name_reason: Compliant with fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain 'pan_cursor' (battle UI camera), descriptor 'to_tile_animated' precisely reflects behavior -- animated pan of the battle cursor to a target tile (target_x,target_y), stepping one tile per frame X-axis first then Y-axis. No Ghidra address residue; no domain-ID suffix to preserve. Distinguishes it from the sibling fd2_pan_cursor_to_char (char-index convenience wrapper) and fd2_pan_cursor_and_window (scrolls window origin instead of cursor).
purpose: Animated battle-cursor camera pan: step the cursor one tile per frame from its current world position toward target tile (target_x, target_y), X-axis first then Y-axis, redrawing each step; used for camera-focus sequences (attack-target highlight, AI move/destination preview, chapter-end cinematics).
logic_summary: composite_battle_frame(0) once up front. Then X loop: while target_x != cursor_world_x, call cursor_move_left() if target_x < cursor_world_x else cursor_move_right(); if anim_phase != 0 && anim_phase != 6, wait_n_bios_ticks(1) (pulse pacing, skipped during phase 0/6 to avoid double-pulsing); clear_keyboard_buffer(). Identical Y loop using cursor_move_up()/cursor_move_down() against cursor_world_y. The directional move handlers themselves clamp at map edges, so callers must pass in-bounds tile coords. Leading __CHK(0x14,...) in the decompile is the Watcom stack-overflow check prologue (CRT artifact), correctly omitted from src.

params.name: target_x
params.semantics: Destination tile column (world X) the cursor should pan to. Compared SIGNED against data_fd2_battle_cursor_world_x to pick left vs right stepping. Caller fd2_pan_cursor_to_char passes runtime_char[char_idx].pos_x, confirming this is a map tile column.
params.reason: Descriptive, matches usage (target tile X), no address residue.

params.name: target_y
params.semantics: Destination tile row (world Y) the cursor should pan to. Compared SIGNED against data_fd2_battle_cursor_world_y to pick up vs down stepping. Caller fd2_pan_cursor_to_char passes runtime_char[char_idx].pos_y, confirming this is a map tile row.
params.reason: Descriptive, matches usage (target tile Y), no address residue.

returns.semantics: No return value; side effect is the animated cursor pan (mutates cursor world/screen position and view window origin via the move handlers, repeatedly composites the battle frame).

notes: Comment kept: existing src block (lines 163-167) 'Animated pan: step cursor one tile per frame, X first then Y.' is correct and precise about purpose+primary logic, matching the deliberate terse style shared by the pan trio (fd2_pan_cursor_to_tile_animated/_to_char/_and_window) in this file. Ghidra plate is the verbose-but-accurate version and is consistent with src (no contradiction) -> plate left untouched. No rename (function name + both param names already compliant). No logic issue: the theoretical infinite loop if target is out of map bounds is precluded by callers passing in-bounds tile coords and is by-design, not a bug. Function-level reads_globals reflects direct accesses in this body; the move handlers (separate functions) touch the screen-pos/window-origin globals.
